races.title: State House, District 15
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Phillip Shepard
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina House since 2011, representing District 15 (Onslow County area). Worked 36 years at the Traffic Management Office at Camp Lejeune and spent 12 years as pastor of Lighthouse Baptist Church. Lives in Jacksonville, NC. Ran in the 2019 special congressional primary and lost.

endorsements.text: The State Employees Association of North Carolina (SEANC) endorsed him in 2014.

cands.gaps: We found no birthplace, hometown upbringing or year he moved to North Carolina. We found no sponsored bills (Ballotpedia's list was empty in the text we had) and no documented actions or statements on data centers, homestead property taxes, land buying by investors or foreign owners, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, police and public order, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His 2014 campaign site themes were general (highway funding, cutting wasteful spending, education and jobs). He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys for 2019 through 2026. We found no land-use or data-center positions, no controversies, no foreign ties, and no endorsements for 2026 or 2024. The only source for this profile was his Ballotpedia page.

local.label: Roots 55: Ballotpedia says he worked 36 years at Camp Lejeune, has served in the NC House since 2011 and lives in Jacksonville, NC, so he has lived in North Carolina for well over 25 years as an adult; his birthplace and upbringing are not stated, so 55 is the minimum the record supports.

cands.name: Christopher Schulte
cands.bio: Psychology professor at Coastal Carolina Community College in Jacksonville, NC, and former mental health counselor. Vice-chair of the Onslow County Democratic Party since 2017. Born in Dayton, Ohio. Has run for the NC House in 2020, 2022, 2024 and 2026 but has not held elected office.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Schulte grew up or when he moved to North Carolina; the only record of his birthplace is Dayton, Ohio. We found no 2026 campaign platform statements, since he did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 survey, and his 2022 survey did not address data centers, property taxes, land buying, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. His 2022 survey mentions only general support for public education investment, Medicaid expansion and mental health care. We found no documented positions on data centers or development, no controversies, and no foreign ties. The only endorsements found were recommendations from informal online voting groups, which we did not treat as notable.
